jobs.title: Head of IT Strategy and Transformation
jobs.description:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.

Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

Head of the IT Strategy and Transformation Office (STO) leads an integrated enterprise capability that connects strategy, architecture, investment planning, delivery excellence, organizational change, and executive governance. The role brings Enterprise Architecture, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile Delivery (LACE), Organizational Change Management, and Executive Governance together into one accountable operating model. Through this leadership, the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation ensures technology investments are strategically aligned, architecturally sound, appropriately prioritized, delivery-ready, and supported through adoption. The role connects enterprise strategy to execution by enabling informed decisions, focusing resources on the highest-value work, and improving transparency, consistency, and accountability for transformation outcomes.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Leads the Integrated IT Strategy & Transformation Office

Sets the strategic agenda and annual operating plan for the STO, unifying architecture, portfolio, delivery, and governance activity behind one coherent enterprise strategy.
Owns the end-to-end operating model connecting strategy formulation, investment funding, architectural standards, delivery execution, and governance decision rights.
Serves as the single executive point of accountability for whether the organization's technology investments collectively advance its strategic priorities — through the quality of the recommendations, architecture, and delivery readiness the STO brings forward, not through unilateral funding authority.
Represents the STO to the executive team, the Investment Council, and Board-level committees, translating strategic intent into well-formed, architected, and delivery-ready investment recommendations for those bodies to decide.

Enterprise Architecture

Directs the definition of enterprise architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and reference architectures that ensure every investment advances one coherent strategy.
Establishes the architecture governance model — including an Architecture Review Board that evaluates major initiatives for strategic fit, technical risk, and reuse before funding is committed — and delegates day-to-day chairmanship of the Board to the Principal Architect.
Owns the technology rationalization and modernization roadmap, reducing redundant platforms and technical debt over time.

Lean Portfolio Management

Directs enterprise investment planning, aligning funding, capacity, and prioritization with strategic themes and value streams.
Facilitates the Investment Council — a standing committee of executive leaders who hold formal decision-making authority over funding, sequencing, and re-prioritization of major initiatives — by preparing prioritized investment recommendations, portfolio trade-off analysis, and capacity/value data for the committee's decisions. The Head of IT Strategy & Transformation does not hold personal or unilateral funding decision rights.
Owns portfolio-level value realization: tracking benefits, cost, and capacity against plan, and reallocating investment as strategic priorities shift.

Agile Delivery (LACE)

Builds and matures enterprise delivery capability through the Lean-Agile Center of Excellence — coaching, engineering practices, and operating model maturity across delivery teams.
Scope note: LACE owns the ways of working and delivery-team practices used to build initiatives; it does not own business-side adoption of the resulting process or operational changes — that responsibility sits with Organizational Change Management, below.
Sets delivery standards and operating cadences (e.g., Program Increment planning, Scrum of Scrums) that give the portfolio a predictable, transparent delivery rhythm.
Establishes delivery KPIs (predictability, flow, quality, cycle time) and drives continuous improvement across delivery teams.

Executive Governance

Personally designs, chairs, and runs the decision forums and escalation paths that connect strategy, investment, architecture, and execution — including cadence, membership, and decision rights for each forum. This is not delegated to a direct-report manager; the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation is the accountable owner of governance.
Ensures every major decision (funding, architecture exception, delivery risk) is made in the right forum, by the right owner, with the right information, and personally facilitates the highest-stakes / executive-level sessions.
Publishes and maintains a governance operating calendar and RACI so accountability is explicit at every level of the model; may be supported by governance/PMO analysts for administration and reporting, but retains direct ownership of the function.
Serves as the escalation point of last resort within the STO for unresolved cross-discipline conflicts (e.g., architecture vs. delivery timeline, portfolio priority disputes).

Organizational Change Management

Owns enterprise-level change leadership for the operational and process-related impacts of major initiatives on the business — how work gets done, roles change, and processes are re-designed — as distinct from LACE's focus on delivery-team ways of working.

Directs the Manager, Organizational Change Management to build and run a repeatable OCM methodology (stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, communication planning, training, and adoption measurement) applied consistently across major initiatives.

Ensures every initiative entering the portfolio carries a change-readiness assessment and a named change plan before it is funded, closing a common gap where technical delivery outpaces organizational readiness.

Personally sponsors change management for the STO's own operating model — leading the organization through the shift to a unified strategy, architecture, portfolio, and governance function, including communication, training, and adoption of new decision rights and cadences.

Partners with HR, Communications, and business-unit leaders to align change plans with broader organizational initiatives and to manage change fatigue across concurrent transformations.

Establishes adoption and sentiment metrics (e.g., stakeholder readiness scores, training completion, adoption rates) and reviews them alongside delivery and portfolio KPIs so change outcomes are tracked with the same rigor as cost and schedule.

Team Leadership and Development

Provides strategic, tactical, and day-to-day direction to the architecture, portfolio, delivery, and change management leads who report into the STO.

Builds a cohesive leadership team across historically separate disciplines, establishing shared metrics, cadence, and a common operating language — while personally modeling the governance standard the team is held to, since the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation owns that discipline directly.

Owns hiring, performance management, coaching, and development planning for direct reports; holds them accountable for the same standard across their functions.

Manages the STO's budget, staffing, and vendor/consulting resources, and ensures adherence to company policy and compliance requirements.

Acts as an escalation point and thought partner for the organization on complex, cross-functional strategy, architecture, portfolio, or delivery problems.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Directly supervises the leaders of Enterprise Architecture, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile Delivery (LACE), and Organizational Change Management, and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. Executive Governance is run by the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation directly and has no dedicated manager. Supervisory responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training team members; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining staff; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing direct reports and their teams; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations and goals; forecasting staffing needs across the STO; and enforcing department policies and procedures.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university required, in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field; Master's degree (MBA or equivalent) preferred.
Minimum 12 years of progressive experience across enterprise architecture, portfolio management, agile delivery, or IT/business strategy.
Minimum 7 years in a leadership role managing multidisciplinary teams and/or a Strategy, Transformation, PMO, or Enterprise Architecture function.
Demonstrated track record building or leading a Lean Portfolio Management model, Agile Center of Excellence, or comparable transformation function.

CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES

SAFe Program Consultant (SPC) or SAFe Agilist required; SAFe Lean Portfolio Management (LPM) certification preferred. TOGAF or equivalent enterprise architecture certification preferred. Prosci Change Management Certification or equivalent OCM credential preferred. PMP, PgMP, or ITIL certification a plus.

Knowledge And Skills

Deep working knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks, Lean Portfolio Management, SAFe or comparable scaled-agile operating models, and executive governance design.
Proven ability to translate enterprise strategy into a funded, architected, and delivery-ready portfolio of initiatives.
Skilled at designing governance forums, decision rights, and operating cadences that hold a large organization accountable without adding bureaucracy.
Strong financial acumen — able to build, defend, and manage a multidisciplinary budget and demonstrate portfolio-level value realization.
Exceptional executive communication and influence skills; able to synthesize complex, cross-functional trade-offs into clear recommendations for senior leadership and the Board.
Experience leading organizational change across historically siloed functions, building one shared operating culture out of separate disciplines.
Hands-on knowledge of organizational change management methodology (e.g., Prosci ADKAR or equivalent) and demonstrated ability to personally sponsor change on high-visibility, enterprise-wide initiatives.

jobs.title: Director, IT
jobs.description:
Overview

The Director, IT is responsible for leading the organization’s IT operations, technology services, and overall IT strategy. This role provides leadership and direction across IT support, infrastructure, systems administration, cybersecurity, identity and access management, and technology operations to ensure reliable, secure, and effective technology services across the organization.

Operating with a high degree of autonomy, the Director, IT establishes priorities, develops and maintains IT standards and processes, manages technology risks, and ensures IT services align with business needs and organizational objectives. This position serves as a senior technology leader and trusted partner to stakeholders across the organization.

This role requires a strong balance of strategic leadership, operational oversight, technical knowledge, and people leadership. The Director, IT is responsible for building a responsive and accountable IT function, driving continuous improvement, and ensuring a consistently positive experience for employees and business partners.

Responsibilities

IT Leadership & Strategy

Develop and execute the IT strategy and roadmap in alignment with organizational priorities and business objectives.
Lead day-to-day IT operations and ensure the effective delivery of reliable, secure, and scalable technology services.
Establish IT policies, standards, processes, and service expectations across the organization.
Assess technology needs and make recommendations regarding systems, infrastructure, applications, and services.
Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, technology capabilities, and the overall employee experience.
Develop and manage IT priorities, initiatives, and projects, balancing business requirements, risk, resources, and cost.
Serve as a senior point of escalation for significant technology, operational, and security matters.
Communicate IT priorities, risks, initiatives, and performance to leadership and key stakeholders.

Service Delivery & Operations

Oversee IT support operations, ensuring timely and effective resolution of incidents and service requests in accordance with established SLAs.
Establish and monitor service delivery standards, performance metrics, and operational priorities.
Ensure effective ticket management, prioritization, escalation, and workload distribution across IT resources.
Drive continuous improvement of IT service management processes and end-user support.
Ensure consistent communication with users and stakeholders regarding significant issues, service interruptions, and resolution timelines.
Evaluate IT service providers and vendors to ensure service quality, responsiveness, and value.

Infrastructure & Systems Administration

Oversee the administration, maintenance, and performance of the organization’s technology infrastructure and systems.
Provide direction for Windows, Microsoft 365, Azure/Entra, networking, endpoint management, and related technologies.
Ensure appropriate standards for system configuration, availability, performance, monitoring, and documentation.
Oversee the lifecycle management of hardware, software, systems, and technology platforms.
Evaluate and implement technology improvements that support business continuity, scalability, and operational efficiency.
Ensure appropriate backup, recovery, and business continuity capabilities are maintained.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Compliance

Provide leadership and oversight for the organization’s cybersecurity program and technology-related risk management.
Establish and maintain appropriate security policies, standards, and controls.
Oversee identity and access management, including Active Directory, Microsoft 365, Azure/Entra, MFA, and role-based access controls.
Monitor and oversee security alerts and incidents using Microsoft Defender and related security platforms.
Lead or coordinate the organization’s response to significant security incidents and technology-related risks.
Partner with internal and external resources to investigate, contain, and remediate security issues as required.
Identify security trends, vulnerabilities, and opportunities to strengthen the organization’s security posture.
Support compliance initiatives and ensure IT practices align with applicable security and compliance requirements, including PCI and SOC controls.

Identity & Access Management

Establish and oversee processes for user provisioning, deprovisioning, and role-based access management.
Ensure access controls are appropriately aligned with employee roles and business requirements.
Oversee the administration of identity platforms, including Active Directory, Microsoft 365, and Azure/Entra ID.
Ensure appropriate use of MFA and other security controls.
Periodically review access, permissions, and administrative privileges to support security and compliance requirements.

Asset, Vendor & Technology Management

Maintain oversight of the organization’s IT asset lifecycle, including hardware, software, licensing, and related technology resources.
Ensure accurate asset and configuration records are maintained.
Develop and manage technology lifecycle and replacement strategies.
Manage relationships with IT vendors, service providers, and technology partners.
Evaluate vendor performance, contracts, licensing, and service agreements.
Support budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning for IT resources and initiatives.

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, mentor, and develop IT staff, providing clear direction, priorities, and performance expectations.
Build a culture of accountability, responsiveness, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Establish appropriate roles, responsibilities, and operating practices within the IT function.
Support professional development, training, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
Recruit and retain IT talent with the skills required to support the organization’s evolving technology needs.
Foster effective collaboration between IT and other departments across the organization.

Business Partnership

Partner with business leaders and functional teams to understand technology needs and identify opportunities to improve business processes.
Translate business requirements into practical technology solutions.
Provide guidance and recommendations to leadership on technology opportunities, risks, and investments.
Support organizational initiatives and projects where technology expertise or resources are required.
Promote effective and responsible use of technology across the organization.

This list of responsibilities might not cover everything you'll end up doing.

Qualifications

Demonstrated ability to lead IT operations and technology services within a business environment.
Proven experience developing and executing IT strategies, roadmaps, and operational plans.
Strong technical knowledge across infrastructure, systems administration, Microsoft technologies, cybersecurity, and end-user computing.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess complex technical and business issues and develop practical solutions.
Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical information effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong organizational, project management, and prioritization skills.
Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining focus on business objectives.
Proven ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and make decisions with limited supervision.
Demonstrated experience leading, mentoring, and developing IT teams.
Strong vendor management and relationship-building skills.

Required Skills & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
7+ years of progressive experience in IT, including demonstrated experience in a leadership or management capacity.
Strong experience with:
Windows 10 and Windows 11 in enterprise environments
Windows Server
Active Directory administration
Microsoft 365 administration
Azure / Entra ID
Microsoft Intune (MDM/MAM)
Exchange Online
Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
Endpoint management and security

Experience with:
ITSM platforms such as ServiceNow
Microsoft Defender and endpoint security technologies
VPN technologies, including Palo Alto GlobalProtect
Networking fundamentals and Cisco technologies
PowerShell scripting and automation
IT asset and lifecycle management
Vendor and technology service management
IT budgeting and technology planning

Working knowledge of:
Cybersecurity and incident response
Business continuity and disaster recovery
Security and compliance frameworks, including PCI and SOC
IT governance, risk management, and security best practices
Cloud technologies and Microsoft Azure

Additional Requirements

Ability to lift and transport equipment up to 40 lbs. as needed.
Ability to participate in occasional after-hours support or incident response activities when required.

We offer a Total Rewards plan designed with you and your family’s health and wellness in mind that includes:

Paid days off ( i. e. vacatio n, sick days, bereavement leave)
Health and Dental plans
Retirement plans
Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP)
Employee referral program

jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in cybersecurity focus on protecting organisations from cyber threats through advanced technologies and strategies. They work to identify vulnerabilities, develop secure systems, and provide proactive solutions to safeguard sensitive data.

In identity and access management at PwC, you will focus on confirming secure and efficient access to systems and data for employees and/or clients. Your work will involve the design and implementation of strategies to protect sensitive information and manage user identities.

Growing as a strategic advisor, you leverage your influence, expertise, and network to deliver quality results. You motivate and coach others, coming together to solve complex problems. As you increase in autonomy, you apply sound judgment, recognising when to take action and when to escalate. You are expected to solve through complexity, ask thoughtful questions, and clearly communicate how things fit together. Your ability to develop and sustain high performing, diverse, and inclusive teams, and your commitment to excellence, contributes to the success of our Firm.

Craft and convey clear, impactful and engaging messages that tell a holistic story.

Apply systems thinking to identify underlying problems and/or opportunities.

Validate outcomes with clients, share alternative perspectives, and act on client feedback.

Direct the team through complexity, demonstrating composure through ambiguous, challenging and uncertain situations.

Deepen and evolve your expertise with a focus on staying relevant.

Initiate open and honest coaching conversations at all levels.

Make difficult decisions and take action to resolve issues hindering team effectiveness.

Model and reinforce professional and technical standards (e.g. refer to specific PwC tax and audit guidance), the Firm's code of conduct, and independence requirements.

As part of the Cybersecurity team you will lead large-scale identity and access management projects, driving innovative solutions that enhance security and operational excellence. As a Senior Manager, you will serve as a strategic advisor, leveraging your knowledge to influence outcomes and build top-performing teams that tackle complex challenges. This role offers the chance to work with advanced technologies and collaborate with clients to develop tailored IAM solutions, securing a significant impact on their security posture.

Build and develop top-performing teams to address complex challenges

Utilize advanced technologies to improve operational effectiveness

Influence project outcomes through knowledgeable guidance and support

Secure alignment with industry standards and regulatory requirements

Bachelor's Degree

7 years of experience

What Sets You Apart

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Computer and Information Science, Cybersecurity, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Information Security, or Management Information Systems preferred

Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Java Developer, or Certified with IAM products including: SailPoint ForgeRock, Ping, Okta, CyberArk, Oracle, or CA preferred

Demonstrating in-depth knowledge of IAM concepts

Utilizing agile development methodologies and DevOps tools

Conducting quantitative and qualitative data analyzes

Managing client engagements and developing business processes

Leading teams to establish direction and motivate members

new_jobs.title: Senior Manager, Global Digital & Technology Systems Engineering
new_jobs.description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

BeOne is a global biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the discovery and development of innovative drug therapies for the treatment of cancer. At BeOne we believe that access to life-changing medicine sees no borders.

The Senior Manager, Global Digital & Technology Systems Engineering is a hands-on technical delivery role within the Systems Engineering capability area, reporting to the Senior Director, Global Digital & Technology Systems Engineering. This role is responsible for executing assigned systems engineering activities across R&D systems, externally developed platforms, integrations, and foundational ML, AI, genAI patterns.

The role translates defined technical standards, architecture direction, implementation plans, and operational expectations into reliable delivery across assigned systems and workstreams. The Senior Manager partners with Global Technology Solutions (Enterprise IT), vendors, R&D stakeholders, and GRDTS peers to ensure solutions align with enterprise infrastructure, cybersecurity, identity management, cloud, operational, and compliance standards.

The Senior Manager contributes practical systems engineering expertise across hybrid cloud, SaaS, high-performance computing (HPC), containerized environments, data pipeline integration, platform observability, and emerging AI architecture patterns including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), secure AI gateway patterns, agentic workflow orchestration, and multi-modal integration patterns. The role focuses on delivery quality, documentation, issue resolution, operational readiness, and sustained technical supportability.

A successful candidate brings strong technical execution skills, pharmaceutical / biotechnology domain awareness, disciplined delivery practices, and the ability to coordinate day-to-day work across business, vendor, Enterprise IT, and technical contributors. The Senior Manager is expected to raise risks and dependencies early, provide transparent execution updates, and help ensure assigned systems engineering work is scalable, secure, compliant, and fit for R&D scientific and business use.

As ours is a growing team, candidates may be evaluated for other suitable levels.

Essential Functions Of The Job

Enterprise IT Alignment & Collaboration

Execute assigned tasks within the Enterprise IT engagement model, coordinating with Global Technology Solutions to align R&D solutions with infrastructure, cybersecurity, identity management, cloud platform, and operational standards.
Support technical design reviews, implementation dependency tracking, access / environment coordination, and issue resolution with Enterprise IT, vendors, and R&D stakeholders.
Document specialized R&D technical needs, constraints, risks, and exceptions for review by the Associate Director and Senior Director.

Platforms & Systems Engineering

Manage assigned systems engineering activities across on-premises, hybrid cloud, vendor-hosted, and multi-tenant SaaS environments, applying standards established for the Systems Engineering capability area.
Develop and maintain technical documentation, integration designs, deployment plans, environment details, runbooks, and platform lifecycle artifacts for assigned systems or workstreams.
Coordinate secure data, digital, and technology integration activities that connect third-party platforms, internal systems, and scientific data flows across defined R&D processes.
Implement observability, telemetry, monitoring, alerting, and supportability practices for assigned systems to improve reliability, performance, and operational readiness.
Support configuration, deployment, validation readiness, and operational handoff activities for high-performance computing clusters, containerized environments, storage layers, data lakes, and pipelines supporting compute-heavy R&D use cases.
Track and execute technical lifecycle activities for assigned systems, including patch coordination, release preparation, codebase / configuration documentation, automated deployment inputs, and transition to steady-state support.

Foundational AI Architectures & Workflow Patterns

Implement assigned components of RAG architectures, vector store integrations, semantic retrieval layers, chunking strategies, and AI-enabled systems under the direction of the Associate Director and Senior Director.
Support reusable implementation patterns for agentic AI workflows, secure AI gateway integrations, multi-agent orchestration, and integration controls consistent with enterprise security and intellectual property protections.
Assist in engineering integration patterns that allow systems to ingest, process, and reason across diverse data types and multi-modal inputs and outputs while maintaining appropriate controls and compliance expectations.

Change Management & Digital Adoption

Execute technical change activities for assigned infrastructure modernization, cloud migration, integration, and platform adoption workstreams in collaboration with Global Technology Solutions and R&D stakeholders.
Prepare and maintain technical impact assessments, adoption inputs, cutover checklists, support handoff materials, and release readiness documentation for leadership review.
Help teams apply consistent integration standards, system documentation practices, and operational readiness expectations across assigned technology workstreams.

Governance & Risk Mitigation
